title: Bhagat Puran Singh
hookLine: a man who carried a disabled boy on his back for years founded the Pingalwara home in Amritsar

cards: Nobody comes back for the boy. He is small, he cannot walk, and someone has left him at the gate of a gurdwara in Lahore. The man who finds him is a sevadar there, a volunteer who sweeps floors and carries water.
His name is Puran Singh. He picks the boy up. Then, the story goes, he simply doesn't put him down.
For years he carries the boy on his back wherever he goes: to the gurdwara, through the streets, to the library where he likes to read.
When the border comes, the two of them cross it together, into a refugee camp in Amritsar.

teach.h: A BOY NOBODY CAME BACK FOR.
teach.b: First, the boy. People who tell the story give him the name Piara, beloved. He couldn't care for himself, and nobody else would.
Puran Singh had no money, no home of his own and no organization. He had a back. Second, the carrying.
This is the part people remember, and it's very plain.
He fed the boy, washed him and carried him, day after day, for years. No committee decided it. No one paid him.
Third, the home. In Amritsar after Partition, Puran Singh began taking in others nobody wanted: the disabled, the abandoned, the dying, people left in the streets.

teach.h: PINGALWARA: A HOME FOR THE UNWANTED.
teach.b: Out of that grew the Pingalwara, a home for them, which still cares for people in Amritsar. People began calling him Bhagat, which means devotee. Nobody appointed him; people saw how he lived.
At Ang 26 of the Guru Granth Sahib, Guru Nanak says that it is by serving in this world that a person finds a place of honor in God's court.

Puran Singh's life reads like that line acted out: seva without a stage, without a sign on the door, with a boy's arms around his neck. And the city that holds the Golden Temple's kitchen also holds the house he built.

how: Sikhs remember Bhagat Puran Singh as an example of seva, and the Pingalwara in Amritsar, the home he founded, still cares for disabled and destitute people, supported by volunteers and donors.

games.q: you're a volunteer at a gurdwara in Lahore. a boy who can't walk is left at the gate, and nobody comes back for him. what do you do?
o: report him and go back to sweeping.
pick him up, and keep carrying him.
wait for someone with money to take charge.
games.why: Puran Singh picked him up and carried him for years, and later founded the Pingalwara in Amritsar.

practice: Feel the weight of your body on the chair or the floor, and notice your back, what it holds up all day without being asked.

Now bring to mind one person near you who is carrying something heavy, an illness, a child, a debt, grief, a job that's too much; breathe in and feel their weight beside your own, breathe out and wonder which small corner of it you could lift.
If you pray, hold them in Waheguru.
